## Overview

The Go team published a detailed explainer on November 4 titled ["A new Go API for JSON"](https://go.dev/blog/jsonv2), walking through why `encoding/json/v2` and its companion `encoding/json/jsontext` package depart from the two-decade-old `encoding/json` package's behavior. The [post](https://go.dev/blog/jsonv2) is billed as "an updated version of the article introducing the experiment," expanding on an experimental API the team first wrote about in 2025 that reached stable, genera...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-organized News follow-up (713 words, within the 400-1200 News range) structured around Overview / What the post adds / Compatibility stance unchanged / What We Don't Know. Neutral tone throughout; no sensationalism or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns) and both hosts (go.dev, pkg.go.dev) are on config/source_allowlist.txt, so no allowlist action is needed. Read source-0.html.gz (go.dev/blog/jsonv2, the Nov 4 2026 'A new Go API for JSON' post, byline Michael Pratt/Joe Tsai/Daniel Martí/Johan Brandhorst-Satzkorn/Roger Peppe/Chris Hines/Damien Neil) in full after gunzip+HTML-strip and verified sha256 8dcefa8b81d7efd5edad889bbc6d1b444c62e293ec44b52ad0853bbff6d7a242 matches the manifest. Read source-1.html.gz (pkg.go.dev/encoding/json/v2) in full, verified sha256 b84afe284ba5251ef7fb4e95d2b53044b1eaed8b3f9ec4c2457e73c937670a46 matches the manifest. CVE-2017-12635 citation confirmed verbatim in source-0: 'This could be exploited by attackers in security applications and has been exploited before (as in CVE-2017-12635).' The 10x Unmarshal speedup claim confirmed verbatim: 'The Unmarshal performance of v2 is significantly faster than v1, with benchmarks demonstrating improvements of up to 10x.' The kube-openapi#315 example confirmed verbatim: 'recursive parsing of OpenAPI specifications in UnmarshalJSON methods significantly hurt performance in a particular service of Kubernetes (see kubernetes/kube-openapi#315), while switching to UnmarshalJSONFrom improved performance by orders of magnitude.' The 'about 6 years' timeline, the 'late 2020' Martí draft, the GopherCon talk/discussion 'posted in late 2023', the 'formal proposal posted in early 2025', the Go 1.25 experiment adoption, and the full contributor name list (Roger Peppe, Chris Hines, Johan Brandhorst-Satzkorn, Damien Neil, Austin Clements, Michael Pratt) all confirmed verbatim against source-0. The pkg.go.dev quotes ('generally chooses more secure defaults than v1, but care should still be taken with large integers or unknown members' and 'ignore unknown names and their corresponding values') confirmed verbatim against source-1. I independently reread this PR's final submitted text against the raw source for a literal quote-by-quote check (per the reviewer brief's warning that recent batches had REJECTs for paraphrased/altered quotes) and found two quotes that are NOT verbatim as presented: (1) the article quotes v1 as accepting invalid UTF-8 'whereas RFC 8259 requires valid UTF-8' but the source's actual sentence is 'whereas the latest Internet Standard (RFC 8259) requires valid UTF-8' — words were dropped from inside the quotation marks without an ellipsis; (2) the article quotes 'both the original encoding/json and new encoding/json/v2 packages are subject to the Go 1 compatibility promise' but the source's actual sentence is 'The original encoding/json and new encoding/json/v2 packages are of course both subject to the Go 1 compatibility promise' — 'both' was moved from mid-sentence to the front and 'of course' was dropped, again inside quotation marks with no ellipsis. Neither alteration changes the substantive meaning of the claim, and both are subordinate body claims, not the headline/summary/lead. Also flagged: the Overview's description of encoding/json as a 'two-decade-old' package is not supported by the source, which says only that JSON support existed 'since well before Go 1.0' and that the team 'first wrote about support for JSON in Go more than 15 years ago' (Go itself was announced publicly in Nov 2009, so the package cannot be ~20 years old as of this Nov 2026 post; 15-17 years is the figure the source itself supports). This is a descriptive aside, not part of the headline or summary, and does not affect the article's central claims (the CVE, the 10x figure, and the six-year dev timeline, all of which check out exactly). Filing a corrections record for all three items rather than REJECT, since a single honest corrections note can cover them and none touches the headline/summary/lead. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article is about the Go team and standard library internals; Anthropic/Claude is not the subject and does not appear in the headline/summary/lead.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline and summary check out exactly: Nov 4 publish date confirmed ('4 November 2026' byline date), CVE-2017-12635 confirmed, 'up to 10x' Unmarshal speedup confirmed, 'about 6 years' development timeline confirmed. Absence claims in the 'What We Don't Know' section (no adoption figures disclosed, no further follow-up posts specified) were checked against the full text of both snapshots and hold up - neither source discloses adoption numbers or a schedule for further Go 1.27 follow-up posts. See source_verification above for the three recoverable issues found (two altered quotes, one imprecise 'two-decade-old' age characterization).

editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate and well-sourced News follow-up; the CVE, the 10x Unmarshal figure, and the six-year development history all check out verbatim against the raw go.dev and pkg.go.dev snapshots, and this is a genuine new follow-up to the August 20 Go 1.27 article, not a duplicate. Two subordinate quotes were altered from the source without an ellipsis and one descriptive aside overstates the age of encoding/json; none touches the headline, summary, or lead, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a three-item corrections record is the right call rather than REJECT.
